newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends sharply up.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate ended sharply higher on Friday as banks adopted a cautious policy in the first trading day of the new monthly reserve period, dealers said.
The overnight rate closed at 6.405 percent against Thursday's 5.838 close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was stable at 6.00-6.25 percent against 6.00-6.50.
Dealers said a red hot stock market added caution over tightening liquidity as funds have persistently flowed out of the banking system to the local bourse.
On Friday the stock index, flush with momentum from Wall Street's record rally overnight, closed 1.83 percent or 164.94 points higher at 9,192.57 to reach a seven-year high.
The central bank's attitude would determine the money rates next week, dealers said.
Government bond yields rose as investors dumped bond holdings for shares in the stock market.
The benchmark 86/4 bond yield was traded at 5.8850 percent in the earlier session against Thursday's 5.8690-8700 close.
